cops.description: Checks for duplicate gem entries in Gemfile.
Checks for duplicate group entries in Gemfile.
Add a comment describing each gem.
Enforces the filename for managing gems.
Requires or forbids specifying gem versions.

The source `:gemcutter`, `:rubygems` and `:rubyforge` are deprecated because HTTP requests are insecure. Please change your source to 'https://rubygems.org' if possible, or 'http://rubygems.org' if not.
Gems within groups in the Gemfile should be alphabetically sorted.
Prefer `add_dependency` over `add_runtime_dependency`.
Use consistent style for Gemspec attributes assignment.
Requires or forbids specifying gem dependency versions.
Checks that deprecated attribute assignments are not set in a gemspec file.
Checks that development dependencies are specified in Gemfile rather than gemspec.
An attribute assignment method calls should be listed only once in a gemspec.
Dependencies in the gemspec should be alphabetically sorted.
Checks that the gemspec has metadata to require Multi-Factor Authentication from RubyGems.
Checks that `required_ruby_version` of gemspec is specified and equal to `TargetRubyVersion` of .rubocop.yml.
Checks usage of RUBY_VERSION in gemspec.
Checks indentation of private/protected visibility modifiers.
Align the arguments of a method call if they span more than one line.
Align the elements of an array literal if they span more than one line.
Checks the indentation of the first line of the right-hand-side of a multi-line assignment.
Align ends corresponding to begins correctly.
Align block ends correctly.
Put end statement of multiline block on its own line.
Checks how the `when` and `in` clauses of a `case` expression are indented.
Enforces a configured order of definitions within a class body.
Checks the indentation of here document closings.
Checks the indentation of hanging closing parentheses.
Checks the indentation of comments.
Checks for condition placed in a confusing position relative to the keyword.
Align ends corresponding to defs correctly.
Checks the position of the dot in multi-line method calls.
Align elses and elsifs correctly.
Checks empty comment.
Add empty line after guard clause.
Add an empty line after magic comments to separate them from code.
Enforces empty line after multiline condition.
Use empty lines between class/module/method defs.
Don't use several empty lines in a row.
Keeps track of empty lines after module inclusion methods.
Keep blank lines around access modifiers.
Keeps track of empty lines around method arguments.
Keep blank lines around attribute accessors.
Keeps track of empty lines around begin-end bodies.
Keeps track of empty lines around block bodies.
Keeps track of empty lines around class bodies.
Keeps track of empty lines around exception handling keywords.
Keeps track of empty lines around method bodies.
Keeps track of empty lines around module bodies.
Align ends correctly.
Use Unix-style line endings.
Do not use unnecessary spacing.
Checks the indentation of the first argument in a method call.
Checks the indentation of the first element in an array literal.
Checks for a line break before the first element in a multi-line array.
Checks the indentation of the first key in a hash literal.
Checks for a line break before the first element in a multi-line hash.
Checks for a line break before the first argument in a multi-line method call.
Checks for a line break before the first parameter in a multi-line method parameter definition.
Checks the indentation of the first parameter in a method definition.
Align the elements of a hash literal if they span more than one line.
Checks for the placement of the closing parenthesis in a method call that passes a HEREDOC string as an argument.
Checks the indentation of the here document bodies.
Keep indentation straight.
Consistent indentation either with tabs only or spaces only.
Use 2 spaces for indentation.
Checks the indentation of the first non-blank non-comment line in a file.
Comments should start with a space.
Checks for unnecessary blank lines at the beginning of a file.
Use trailing spaces instead of leading spaces in strings broken over multiple lines (by a backslash).
Checks the spacing in front of backslash in line continuations.
Checks the indentation of the next line after a line that ends with a string literal and a backslash.
Checks that line length does not exceed the configured limit.
Checks that the closing brace in an array literal is either on the same line as the last array element, or a new line.
Checks that each item in a multi-line array literal starts on a separate line.
Checks for a newline after the assignment operator in multi-line assignments.
Ensures newlines after multiline block do statements.
Checks that the closing brace in a hash literal is either on the same line as the last hash element, or a new line.
Checks that each item in a multi-line hash literal starts on a separate line.
Checks that each argument in a multi-line method call starts on a separate line.
Checks that the closing brace in a method call is either on the same line as the last method argument, or a new line.
Checks indentation of method calls with the dot operator that span more than one line.
Checks that the closing brace in a method definition is either on the same line as the last method parameter, or a new line.
Checks that each parameter in a multi-line method definition starts on a separate line.
Checks indentation of binary operations that span more than one line.
Align the parameters of a method definition if they span more than one line.
Do not break up an expression into multiple lines when it fits on a single line.
Align rescues and ensures correctly.
Put method call on a separate line if chained to a single line block.
Use spaces after colons.
Use spaces after commas.
Do not put a space between a method name and the opening parenthesis in a method definition.
Tracks redundant space after the ! operator.
Use spaces after semicolons.
Checks the spacing inside and after block parameters pipes.
Checks that the equals signs in parameter default assignments have or don't have surrounding space depending on configuration.
Use a space around keywords if appropriate.
Checks method call operators to not have spaces around them.
Use a single space around operators.
Checks that the left block brace has or doesn't have space before it.
Checks for receiver with a space before the opening brackets.
No spaces before commas.
Checks for missing space between code and a comment on the same line.
Checks that exactly one space is used between a method name and the first argument for method calls without parentheses.
No spaces before semicolons.
Checks for spaces in lambda literals.
Checks the spacing inside array literal brackets.
No unnecessary additional spaces between elements in %i/%w literals.
Checks that block braces have or don't have surrounding space. For blocks taking parameters, checks that the left brace has or doesn't have trailing space.
Use spaces inside hash literal braces - or don't.
No spaces after ( or before ).
No unnecessary spaces inside delimiters of %i/%w/%x literals.
No spaces inside range literals.
Checks the spacing inside referential brackets.
Checks for padding/surrounding spaces inside string interpolation.
Checks trailing blank lines and final newline.
Avoid trailing whitespace.
Checks for mistyped shorthand assignments.
Checks for ambiguous block association with method when param passed without parentheses.
Checks for ambiguous operators in the first argument of a method invocation without parentheses.
Checks for expressions containing multiple binary operations with ambiguous precedence.
Checks for ranges with ambiguous boundaries.
Checks for ambiguous regexp literals in the first argument of a method invocation without parentheses.
Checks for an array literal interpolated inside a regexp.
Don't use assignment in conditions.
`BigDecimal.new()` is deprecated. Use `BigDecimal()` instead.
Checks for places where binary operator has identical operands.
Checks for `:true` and `:false` symbols.
Default values in optional keyword arguments and optional ordinal arguments should not refer back to the name of the argument.
Do not define constants within a block.
Checks for overwriting an exception with an exception result by use `rescue =>`.
Checks for constant reassignments.
Checks that constants are fully qualified with `::`.
Checks that `# rubocop:` directives are strictly formatted.
Disallow overriding the `Data` built-in methods via `Data.define`.
Checks for debugger calls.
Checks for deprecated class method calls.
Checks for deprecated constants.
Don't use algorithm constants for `OpenSSL::Cipher` and `OpenSSL::Digest`.
In constructor, plain assignment is preferred over disjunctive.
Checks that there are no repeated bodies within `if/unless`, `case-when` and `rescue` constructs.
Do not repeat values in case conditionals.
Do not repeat conditions used in if `elsif`.
Checks for duplicate keys in hash literals.
Checks for duplicated magic comments.
Do not repeat patterns in `in` keywords.
Checks for duplicate method definitions.
Checks for duplicate elements in Regexp character classes.
Checks for duplicate `require`s and `require_relative`s.
Checks that there are no repeated exceptions used in `rescue` expressions.
Checks for duplicate elements in Set.
Checks for immutable argument given to each_with_object.
Checks for odd code arrangement in an else block.
Checks for blocks without a body.
Checks for classes and metaclasses without a body.
Checks for the presence of `if`, `elsif` and `unless` branches without a body.
Checks for empty ensure block.
Checks for empty expressions.
Enforces that Ruby source files are not empty.
Checks for the presence of `in` pattern branches without a body.
Checks for empty string interpolation.
Checks for `when` branches with empty bodies.
Do not use return in an ensure block.
Use `:trim_mode` and `:eoutvar` keyword arguments to `ERB.new`.
Checks for flip-flops.
Checks for the presence of precise comparison of floating point numbers.
Catches floating-point literals too large or small for Ruby to represent.
Checks for a mismatch between the format fields and the arguments to `format`/`sprintf`/`%`.
Prefer using `Hash#compare_by_identity` than using `object_id` for keys.
Checks for the deprecated use of keyword arguments for hash default in `Hash.new`.
Checks for the ordering of a method call where the receiver of the call is a HEREDOC.
Prefer `equal?` over `==` when comparing `object_id`.
Checks for adjacent string literals on the same line, which could better be represented as a single string literal.
Checks for `IO.select` that is incompatible with Fiber Scheduler.
Checks for attempts to use `private` or `protected` to set the visibility of a class method, which does not work.
Avoid inheriting from the `Exception` class.
Checks for interpolation in a single quoted string.
Checks uses of `it` calls without arguments in block.
Checks uses of lambda without a literal block.
Checks of literals used in conditions.
Checks for literal assignments in the conditions.
Checks for literals used in interpolation.
Use Kernel#loop with break rather than begin/end/until or begin/end/while for post-loop tests.
Checks for a `# rubocop:enable` after `# rubocop:disable`.
Checks for the presence of constructors and lifecycle callbacks without calls to `super`.
Checks for mixed-case character ranges since they include likely unintended characters.
Do not mix named captures and numbered captures in a Regexp literal.
Use `&&` operator to compare multiple values.
Do not use nested method definitions.
Checks for nested percent literals.
Do not omit the accumulator when calling `next` in a `reduce`/`inject` block.
Do not `return` inside `begin..end` blocks in assignment contexts.
Checks for non-atomic file operations.
Always sort arrays returned by Dir.glob when requiring files.
Do not use return in iterator to cause non-local exit.
Checks unsafe usage of number conversion methods.
Checks for uses of numbered parameter assignment.
Checks for numeric operations with constant results.
Checks unintended or-assignment to constant.
Checks the proper ordering of magic comments and whether a magic comment is not placed before a shebang.
Checks for out of range reference for Regexp because it always returns nil.
Checks for method calls with a space before the opening parenthesis.
Checks for unwanted commas and quotes in %w/%W literals.
Checks for unwanted commas and colons in %i/%I literals.
Checks for `raise` or `fail` statements which are raising `Exception` class.
Checks for `rand(1)` calls. Such calls always return `0` and most likely a mistake.
Checks for rubocop:disable comments that can be removed. Note: this cop is not disabled when disabling all cops. It must be explicitly disabled.
Checks for rubocop:enable comments that can be removed.
Checks for redundant `sort` method to `Dir.glob` and `Dir[]`.
Checks for redundant quantifiers in Regexps.
Checks for unnecessary `require` statement.
Checks for redundant safe navigation calls.
Checks for splat unnecessarily being called on literals.
Checks for Object#to_s usage in string interpolation.
Checks for redundantly converting a literal to the same type.
Checks for redundant `with_index`.
Checks for redundant `with_object`.
Use `Refinement#import_methods` when using `include` or `prepend` in `refine` block.
Do not use regexp literal as a condition. The regexp literal matches `$_` implicitly.
Use parentheses in the method call to avoid confusion about precedence.
Checks that a range literal is enclosed in parentheses when the end of the range is at a line break.
Checks for uses a file requiring itself with `require_relative`.
Avoid rescuing the Exception class.
Avoid rescuing from non constants that could result in a `TypeError`.
Checks for return in void context.
Do not chain ordinary method call after safe navigation operator.

Check to make sure that if safe navigation is used in an `&&` or `||` condition, consistent and appropriate safe navigation, without excess or deficiency, is used for all method calls on the same object.
Avoid `foo&.empty?` in conditionals.
Grant script file execute permission.
Checks for self-assignments.
Checks for `send` method when using mixin.
Avoid reassigning arguments before they were used.
Avoid rescuing a higher level exception before a lower level exception.
Do not use the same name as outer local variable for block arguments or block local variables.
Checks for mutable literals used as default arguments during Hash initialization.
Disallow overriding the `Struct` built-in methods via `Struct.new`.
Don't suppress exceptions.
Checks for cases where exceptions unrelated to the numeric constructors may be unintentionally swallowed.
Checks for unnecessary symbol conversions.
Checks for syntax errors.
Ensures that `to_enum`/`enum_for`, called for the current method, has correct arguments.
Ensure #to_json includes an optional argument.
Detects top level return statements with argument.
Checks for trailing commas in attribute declarations.
Checks for useless triple quote constructs.
Do not use prefix `_` for a variable that is used.
Checks for unescaped literal `]` in Regexp.
Looks for blocks that have fewer arguments that the calling method expects.
Use Integer instead of Fixnum or Bignum.
Checks for `reduce` or `inject` blocks that do not update the accumulator each iteration.
Checks for unreachable code.
Checks for loops that will have at most one iteration.
Checks for unreachable `in` pattern branches after an unconditional catch-all pattern.
Checks for unused block arguments.
Checks for unused method arguments.

`URI.escape` method is obsolete and should not be used. Instead, use `CGI.escape`, `URI.encode_www_form` or `URI.encode_www_form_component` depending on your specific use case. Also `URI.unescape` method is obsolete and should not be used. Instead, use `CGI.unescape`, `URI.decode_www_form` or `URI.decode_www_form_component` depending on your specific use case.
Use `URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.make_regexp` instead of `URI.regexp`.
Checks for useless access modifiers.
Checks for useless assignment to a local variable.
Checks for useless constant scoping.
Checks for usage of `fetch` or `Array.new` with default value argument and block.
Checks for calls to `defined?` with strings and symbols. The result of such a call will always be truthy.
Checks for useless `else` in `begin..end` without `rescue`.
Checks for useless method definitions.
Checks for useless numeric operations.
Checks for useless OR expressions.
Checks for useless `rescue`s.
Finds unnecessary uses of `ruby2_keywords`.
Checks for useless setter call to a local variable.
Checks for useless `Integer#times` calls.
Checks for operators, literals, lambdas, and procs used in void context.
Checks that the ABC size of methods is not higher than the configured maximum.
Avoid long blocks with many lines.
Avoid excessive block nesting.
Avoid classes longer than 100 lines of code.
Checks for `Array` or `Hash` literals with many entries.
Checks that the cyclomatic complexity of methods is not higher than the configured maximum.
Avoid methods longer than 10 lines of code.
Avoid modules longer than 100 lines of code.
Avoid parameter lists longer than three or four parameters.
Checks that the perceived complexity of methods is not higher than the configured maximum.
Checks that cop names in `rubocop:disable` (etc.) comments are given with a department name.
Checks the naming of accessor methods for get_/set_.
Use only ascii symbols in identifiers and constants.
Checks that the sole parameter of binary operator methods is named `other`.
Use anonymous block forwarding.
Checks for block parameter names that contain capital letters, end in numbers, or do not meet a minimal length.
Use CamelCase for classes and modules.
Constants should use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
Use snake_case for source file names.
Use configured case for heredoc delimiters.
Use descriptive heredoc delimiters.
Recommend the use of inclusive language instead of problematic terms.
Memoized method name should match memo instance variable name.
Use the configured style when naming methods.
Checks for method parameter names that contain capital letters, end in numbers, or do not meet a minimal length.
Checks that predicate methods end with `?` and non-predicate methods do not.
Checks that predicate method names end with a question mark and do not start with a forbidden prefix.
Use consistent rescued exceptions variables naming.
Use the configured style when naming variables.
Use the configured style when numbering symbols, methods and variables.
Checks for `hash` implementations that combine values manually instead of delegating to `Array#hash`.
Checks for the use of `Kernel#eval` and `Binding#eval` with dynamic arguments.
Checks for the first argument to `IO.read`, `IO.binread`, `IO.write`, `IO.binwrite`, `IO.foreach`, and `IO.readlines`.
Prefer usage of `JSON.parse` over `JSON.load` due to potential security issues. See reference for more information.
Avoid using of `Marshal.load` or `Marshal.restore` due to potential security issues. See reference for more information.
Checks for the use of `Kernel#open` and `URI.open` with dynamic data.
Prefer usage of `YAML.safe_load` over `YAML.load` due to potential security issues. See reference for more information.
Checks style of how access modifiers are used.
Checks for grouping of accessors in `class` and `module` bodies.
Use alias instead of alias_method.
Checks for endless methods inside operators of lower precedence.
Use &&/|| instead of and/or.
Use arguments forwarding.
Use Array() instead of explicit Array check or [*var], when dealing with a variable you want to treat as an Array, but you're not certain it's an array.
Use `arr.first` and `arr.last` instead of `arr[0]` and `arr[-1]`.
Use `array1.intersect?(array2)` instead of `(array1 & array2).any?`.
Use `include?(element)` instead of `intersect?([element])`.
Use Array#join instead of Array#*.
Use only ascii symbols in comments.
Checks for uses of Module#attr.
Suggests the usage of an auto resource cleanup version of a method (if available).
Checks if usage of %() or %Q() matches configuration.
Avoid the use of BEGIN blocks.
Checks for places where `attr_reader` and `attr_writer` for the same method can be combined into single `attr_accessor`.
Prefer bitwise predicate methods over direct comparison operations.
Do not use block comments.
Avoid using {...} for multi-line blocks (multiline chaining is always ugly). Prefer {...} over do...end for single-line blocks.
Avoid explicit use of the case equality operator (`===`).
Identifies places where `if-elsif` constructions can be replaced with `case-when`.
Checks for uses of character literals.
Checks style of children classes and modules.
Enforces consistent use of `Object#is_a?` or `Object#kind_of?`.
Enforces the use of `Object#instance_of?` instead of class comparison for equality.
Use self when defining module/class methods.
Enforces using `def self.method_name` or `class << self` to define class methods.
Avoid the use of class variables.
Use `{Array,Hash}#{compact,compact!}` instead of custom logic to reject nils.
Enforces the use of consistent method names from the `Enumerable` module.
Prefer `Enumerable` predicate methods over expressions with `count`.
Do not use :: for method call.
Do not use :: for defining class methods.
Checks successive `defined?` calls that can be combined into a single call.
Checks for places where multiple consecutive loops over the same data can be combined into a single loop.
Use `` or %x around command literals.
Checks formatting of special comments (TODO, FIXME, OPTIMIZE, HACK, REVIEW, NOTE).
Do not place comments on the same line as certain keywords.
Enforces the use of `Comparable#between?` instead of logical comparison.
Enforces the use of `Comparable#clamp` instead of comparison by minimum and maximum.
Enforces the use of `Array#push(item)` instead of `Array#concat([item])` to avoid redundant array literals.
Use the return value of `if` and `case` statements for assignment to a variable and variable comparison instead of assigning that variable inside of each branch.
Check that class- and module constants have visibility declarations.
Include a copyright notice in each file before any code.
Checks for inheritance from Data.define.
Use Time over DateTime.
Use def with parentheses when there are arguments.
Use `dig` with multiple parameters instead of chaining multiple calls.
Use the `__dir__` method to retrieve the canonicalized absolute path to the current file.
Prefer to use `Dir.empty?('path/to/dir')` when checking if a directory is empty.
Forbids disabling/enabling cops within source code.
When using `class_eval` (or other `eval`) with string interpolation, add a comment block showing its appearance if interpolated.
Document classes and non-namespace modules.
Checks for missing documentation comment for public methods.
Checks for double rubocop:disable comments on a single line.
Checks for uses of double negation (!!).
Use `Integer#times` for a simple loop which iterates a fixed number of times.
Prefer `each_with_object` over `inject` or `reduce`.
Omit pipes for empty block parameters.
Avoid empty condition in case statements.
Enforces consistent style for empty class definitions.
Avoid empty else-clauses.
Checks for using empty heredoc to reduce redundancy.
Omit parens for empty lambda parameters.
Prefer literals to Array.new/Hash.new/String.new.
Checks the formatting of empty method definitions.
Checks for empty strings being assigned inside string interpolation.
Use UTF-8 as the source file encoding.
Avoid the use of END blocks.
Avoid the use of multi-lined endless method definitions.
Checks for consistent usage of `ENV['HOME']`.
Pass `__FILE__` and `__LINE__` to `eval` method, as they are used by backtraces.
Favor the use of `Integer#even?` && `Integer#odd?`.
Checks for exact regexp match inside Regexp literals.
Use `expand_path(__dir__)` instead of `expand_path('..', __FILE__)`.
Consider using explicit block argument to avoid writing block literal that just passes its arguments to another block.
Enforces consistency in the use of exponential (scientific) notation.
Suggests `ENV.fetch` for the replacement of `ENV[]`.
Prefer to use `File.empty?('path/to/file')` when checking if a file is empty.
Use `File::NULL` instead of hardcoding "dev/null".
Checks for `File.open` without a block, which can leak file descriptors.
Favor `File.(bin)read` convenience methods.
Favor `FileUtils.touch` for touching files.
Favor `File.(bin)write` convenience methods.
For performing float division, coerce one side only.
Checks use of for or each in multiline loops.
Enforce the use of Kernel#sprintf, Kernel#format or String#%.
Use a consistent style for format string tokens.
Add the frozen_string_literal comment to the top of files to help transition to frozen string literals by default.
Enforces the use of `$stdout/$stderr/$stdin` instead of `STDOUT/STDERR/STDIN`.
Do not introduce global variables.
Checks for conditionals that can be replaced with guard clauses.
Checks for presence or absence of braces around hash literal as a last array item depending on configuration.
Avoid Hash[] in favor of ary.to_h or literal hashes.
Use Hash#each_key and Hash#each_value.
Checks for usages of `Hash#reject`, `Hash#select`, and `Hash#filter` methods that can be replaced with `Hash#except` method.
Use `Hash#dig` instead of chained `fetch` calls.
Checks for places where `case-when` represents a simple 1:1 mapping and can be replaced with a hash lookup.
Enforces the use of either `Hash#[]` or `Hash#fetch` for hash lookup.
Checks for usages of `Hash#reject`, `Hash#select`, and `Hash#filter` methods that can be replaced with `Hash#slice` method.
Prefer Ruby 1.9 hash syntax { a: 1, b: 2 } over 1.8 syntax { :a => 1, :b => 2 }.
Prefer `transform_keys` over `each_with_object`, `map`, or `to_h`.
Prefer `transform_values` over `each_with_object`, `map`, or `to_h`.
Checks that conditional statements do not have an identical line at the end of each branch, which can validly be moved out of the conditional.
Finds if nodes inside else, which can be converted to elsif.
Favor modifier if/unless usage when you have a single-line body.
Avoid modifier if/unless usage on conditionals.
Checks for redundant `if` with boolean literal branches.
Do not use if x; .... Use the ternary operator instead.
Use `raise` or `fail` with an explicit exception class and message, rather than just a message.
Checks for `in;` uses in `case` expressions.
Use Kernel#loop for infinite loops. This cop is unsafe if the body may raise a `StopIteration` exception.
Avoid trailing inline comments.
Use the inverse method instead of `!.method` if an inverse method is defined.
Favor `if` with inverted condition over `unless`.
Don't include literal IP addresses in code.
Checks for local variables and method parameters named `it`.
Checks for blocks with one argument where `it` block parameter can be used.
When passing an existing hash as keyword arguments, provide additional arguments directly rather than using `merge`.
Enforces that optional keyword parameters are placed at the end of the parameters list.
Use the new lambda literal syntax for single-line blocks.
Use lambda.call(...) instead of lambda.(...).
Use \ instead of + or << to concatenate two string literals at line end.
Use a consistent style for magic comments.
Prefer `select` or `reject` over `map { ... }.compact`.
Checks for usages of `each` with `<<`, `push`, or `append` which can be replaced by `map`.
Checks for redundant `map(&:to_s)` before `join`.
Prefer `to_h` with a block over `map.to_h`.
Prefer `to_set` with a block over `map.to_set`.
Use parentheses for method calls with arguments.
Do not use parentheses for method calls with no arguments.
Avoid chaining a method call on a do...end block.
Checks if the method definitions have or don't have parentheses.
Use `Enumerable#minmax` instead of `Enumerable#min` and `Enumerable#max` in conjunction.
Enforces the use of `max` or `min` instead of comparison for greater or less.

Require if/case expressions to have an else branches. If enabled, it is recommended that Style/UnlessElse and Style/EmptyElse be enabled. This will conflict with Style/EmptyElse if Style/EmptyElse is configured to style "both".
Checks if `method_missing` is implemented without implementing `respond_to_missing`.
Checks for grouping of mixins in `class` and `module` bodies.
Checks that `include`, `extend` and `prepend` exists at the top level.
Checks for usage of `extend self` in modules.
Checks for usage of `Module` methods returning arrays that can be replaced with equivalent predicates.
Avoid multi-line chains of blocks.
Checks for uses of `if`/`unless` modifiers with multiline bodies.
Do not use then for multi-line if/unless.
Do not use `then` for multi-line `in` statement.
Wrap multiline memoizations in a `begin` and `end` block.
Avoid multi-line method signatures.
Avoid multi-line ?: (the ternary operator); use if/unless instead.
Do not use then for multi-line when statement.
Avoid comparing a variable with multiple items in a conditional, use Array#include? instead.
Do not assign mutable objects to constants.
Favor unless over if for negative conditions (or control flow or).
Checks for uses of `if-else` and ternary operators with a negated condition which can be simplified by inverting condition and swapping branches.
Favor if over unless for negative conditions.
Favor until over while for negative conditions.

Use negative array indices instead of calculating array length minus a value. Also handles range patterns with length calculations. Recognizes preserving methods and their combinations, allowing safe replacement when the receiver matches.
Checks for nested `File.dirname`.
Avoid using nested modifiers.
Parenthesize method calls which are nested inside the argument list of another parenthesized method call.
Use one expression per branch in a ternary operator.
Use `next` to skip iteration instead of a condition at the end.
Prefer x.nil? to x == nil.
Prefer `-> {}` to `-> { nil }`.
Checks for redundant nil checks.
Use ! instead of not.
Restrict the usage of numbered parameters.
Avoid excessive numbered params in a single block.
Use smallcase prefixes for numeric literals.
Add underscores to large numeric literals to improve their readability.
Checks for the use of predicate- or comparison methods for numeric comparisons.
Enforces the use of consistent method names `Object#yield_self` or `Object#then`.
Checks that each source file defines at most one top-level class or module.
Favor the ternary operator (?:) or multi-line constructs over single-line if/then/else/end constructs.
Avoid using OpenStruct. As of Ruby 3.0, use is officially discouraged due to performance, version compatibility, and potential security issues.
Checks for redundant dot before operator method call.
Don't use option hashes when you can use keyword arguments.
Checks for optional arguments that do not appear at the end of the argument list.
Use keyword arguments when defining method with boolean argument.
Recommend usage of double pipe equals (||=) where applicable.
